examples.en: We eat the meat together with lettuce.
You wrap samgyeopsal in lettuce to eat it.
I wash the lettuce clean and put it on a plate.
I grow lettuce on my balcony.
Excuse me, could I have some more lettuce?

explain: 상추 잎은 한 장, 두 장으로 세요. 많이 살 때는 한 봉지, 한 단으로 말해요.
explain_en: Lettuce leaves are counted with 장: 한 장, 두 장. When buying a lot, you say 한 봉지 (a bag) or 한 단 (a bunch).

examples.en: I bought purple flowers.
My friend dyed her hair purple.
The skin of a grape is purple.
I often wear purple socks.

examples.ko: 아이가 블루베리를 먹어서 입이 보라색이 됐어요.
examples.en: The child ate blueberries, so their mouth turned purple.

explain: 보라색은 파란색에 가까운 보라예요. 붉은 느낌이 더 많은 보라는 “자주색”이라고 해요.

dict_examples.en: The painter painted the wall purple.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 보라색 is a purple leaning toward blue. A redder purple is called 자주색.

examples.en: The pink hat is pretty.
In spring, pink cherry blossoms come out.
The baby's shoes are pink.
Is this ribbon red? — No, it's pink.
I bought ten pink balloons.

explain: “핑크”나 “핑크색”도 일상에서 자주 써요. 분홍색은 한국어 단어이고 핑크는 영어에서 왔어요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: If you mix white with red, it becomes pink.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 핑크 and 핑크색 are also used in everyday talk. 분홍색 is the Korean word; 핑크 comes from English.

dis.h: standard word with the color suffix

p.n: Same meaning; 핑크 is a casual loanword, often for fashion and brands.

examples.en: Tangerines are orange.
My phone case is orange.
Carrots are orange and taste sweet.
The evening sky is orange.
Where did you buy that orange bag?

explain: “오렌지색”도 많이 써요. 주황색은 한국어 단어이고 오렌지색은 영어 orange에서 왔어요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 오렌지색 is also common. 주황색 is the Korean word; 오렌지색 comes from English “orange”.

dis.h: orange as a color; full standard noun

p.n: 주황 is the shorter form without 색; the meaning is the same.

examples.ko: 우리 집 앞에 회색 고양이가 자주 와요.
examples.en: A gray cat often comes by in front of our house.
The sky is gray today. Do you think it'll rain?
The sky is full of gray clouds.
My coat is gray and my shoes are black.
A gray hoodie is comfortable, so I wear it often.

explain: 회색의 “회”는 재(ash)를 뜻하는 한자예요. 그래서 회색은 재의 색이에요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: The 회 in 회색 is a Chinese character meaning ash. So 회색 is literally the color of ash.

examples.en: I wore a sky-blue T-shirt.
We painted the baby's room sky blue.
The child's bed blanket is light blue.
Please give me just one light blue balloon.
I wore a light blue shirt to the interview.

explain: 한국어에서는 연한 파란색을 보통 “하늘색”이라고 따로 불러요. 짙은 파란색은 “남색”이라고 해요.

dict_examples.en: The sky-blue dress looks really cool and fresh.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Korean usually gives light blue its own name, 하늘색. A dark navy blue is called 남색.

examples.en: I bought white rice cakes at the market.
After we moved in, we handed out rice cakes to the neighbors.
I had rice cake and milk in the morning.

examples.ko: 선물하려고 가게에서 떡을 한 상자 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a box of rice cakes at the shop as a gift.
I grill the rice cake and dip it in honey.

explain: 떡은 종류가 아주 많아요. 송편, 가래떡, 인절미도 모두 떡이에요.

phrases.example: 돈이 없어서 그 비싼 가방은 그림의 떡이에요.
phrases.en: pie in the sky; something you want but can't have
phrases.nuance_ko: 보기만 하고 가질 수 없는 것
phrases.nuance_en: describes something you can only look at and cannot have
phrases.en_equiv: pie in the sky; something you want but can't have

explain_en: There are many kinds of 떡. 송편, 가래떡 and 인절미 are all 떡.

examples.en: On the morning of Lunar New Year, we eat tteokguk.

examples.ko: 떡국을 먹으면 한 살 더 먹어요.
examples.en: When you eat tteokguk, you turn a year older.
I put dumplings in the tteokguk and eat it.
I ordered a bowl of tteokguk at the restaurant.

examples.ko: 떡국은 맵지 않아서 아이들도 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: Tteokguk isn't spicy, so children eat it well too.

explain: 한국에서는 설날 아침에 떡국을 먹어요. ‘떡국을 먹으면 한 살 더 먹는다’고 해서, 나이를 장난스럽게 물을 때 ‘떡국 몇 그릇 먹었어요?’라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: In Korea, people eat 떡국 on the morning of Lunar New Year. Since eating it is said to make you a year older, people sometimes joke '떡국 몇 그릇 먹었어요?' (How many bowls of tteokguk have you eaten?) to ask someone's age.

examples.en: Seolleongtang has a milky white broth.
On cold days I crave a hot bowl of seolleongtang.
Please put lots of green onion in my seolleongtang.
I had seolleongtang near my office at lunch.
Excuse me, two bowls of seolleongtang, please.

explain: 설렁탕은 맛이 싱거워서 보통 소금과 후추로 간을 해서 먹어요.

dict_examples.ko: 우리 점심에 설렁탕이나 한 그릇 먹자.
dict_examples.en: Let's have a bowl of seolleongtang for lunch.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그녀는 며칠 전부터 설렁탕 국물이 먹고 싶다고 남편에게 말했다.
dict_examples.en: She told her husband that she had wanted seolleongtang broth for the past few days.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Seolleongtang is mild, so people usually season it themselves with salt and pepper.

examples.en: Sundubu-jjigae is a little spicy.
I crack an egg into my sundubu-jjigae.
The soft tofu stew is hot, so please eat slowly.
Please make the soft tofu stew not spicy.

examples.ko: 순두부찌개를 시키면 밥하고 반찬이 같이 나와요.
examples.en: If you order the soft tofu stew, rice and side dishes come with it.

explain: 순두부는 굳히기 전의 부드러운 두부예요. 찌개는 국보다 국물이 적고 진해요.

dict_examples.ko: 순두부찌개에 청양고추를 썰어 넣으니 얼큰한 맛이 배가 되었다.
dict_examples.en: When I sliced cheongyang chili peppers into the sundubu-jjigae, the spicy flavor doubled.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 순두부 is soft tofu before it is pressed firm. 찌개 is a stew with less, thicker broth than a 국 (soup).

examples.en: Fried food is best while it's warm.
I dip the fried snacks in the tteokbokki sauce.
We ordered tteokbokki and fried snacks at the snack shop.
Fried food is oily, so I only eat a little.
Two fried shrimp, please.

explain: 튀김은 “튀기다”(deep-fry)에서 나온 말이에요. 새우튀김, 야채튀김처럼 재료 뒤에 붙여요.
explain_en: 튀김 comes from the verb 튀기다 (to deep-fry). Put the ingredient before it: 새우튀김, 야채튀김.

examples.en: The clerk showed me a white bag.
I asked the clerk the price.

examples.ko: 이 옷 가게 점원은 아주 친절해요.
examples.en: The clerks at this clothes shop are very kind.
I work as a clerk at a convenience store.
The clerk brought me another color.

explain: ‘점원’은 가게에서 일하는 사람을 말하는 글말이에요. 직접 부를 때는 ‘점원님’이라고 하지 않고 ‘저기요’나 ‘사장님’이라고 해요. 요즘은 ‘직원’이라는 말을 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: '점원' is a written-style word for a shop worker. When calling one, don't say '점원님'; say '저기요' (excuse me) or '사장님'. These days '직원' is used more often.
